title: Recovering a UK children's charity's website from web archives
audience: Trustees or managers of a small charity whose old website is broken, lost or expensive to keep running.

intent.primary: Can a lost or broken charity website be recovered and rebuilt cheaply, and what does it involve?
related: Can you recover a website from the Wayback Machine?
How do you move a charity off WordPress?

uniqueValue: Shows a real recovery: how many archived addresses were found, how many pages were rescued, and how the rebuild removed the running costs. The Labs page covers the build; this page is for the charity deciding whether to ask.

seo.title: Charity website recovery case study | Chris Demetriou
seo.description: How a UK children's charity's website was recovered from web archives and rebuilt as a fast static site that is free to host.

role.summary: I recovered the site from web archives and rebuilt it.

claims.text: 342 saved addresses were listed in the Wayback Machine and 154 pages were rescued.
The site was rebuilt as a static site: fast, and free to host. WordPress itself was left behind.
Python scripts stripped the archive toolbar, rebuilt the links and made a static copy.

body.text: Yes, if enough of it was archived. For this UK children's charity, 342 saved addresses were listed in the Wayback Machine and 154 pages were rescued, then rebuilt as a static site that is fast and free to host.

body.heading: How the recovery worked
body.text: Scripts stripped the archive toolbar from every saved page, rebuilt the links between pages and produced a clean static copy. WordPress itself was left behind, so there are no plugins to update.
